prompt: Measuring in degrees, what is the period of $y = \sin x$ — the horizontal distance before the wave repeats itself?
hint: Sine values come from going around the unit circle. When does the trip start over?

hints.text: Sine values come from going around the unit circle. When does the trip start over?
You return to the same point after one full lap.
One full lap is $360^\circ$, so the period of $y = \sin x$ is $360^\circ$.

explanation: Each value of $\sin x$ is the height of a point traveling around the unit circle.
After one complete lap you are back at the same point with the same height, so the graph repeats.
A lap is $360^\circ$ (or $2\pi$ radians), so that is the period.

alternativeExplanations.title: Trace the graph
steps: From $0^\circ$ the sine curve rises to 1 at $90^\circ$, falls to 0 at $180^\circ$, drops to $-1$ at $270^\circ$, and returns to 0 at $360^\circ$.
Only at $360^\circ$ is it both back at zero AND heading upward again — a full cycle.
Careful: $180^\circ$ returns to zero but is heading DOWN, so it is only half a cycle.
